title: Inside a Neural Network Layer
description: Move seven sliders and watch a neural network layer's weighted sum and sigmoid activation recompute live.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Foundations
chapter_title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Foundations

educational.learningObjective: Given a small neural network layer with adjustable input values and weights, the learner will compute the weighted sum, apply an activation function, and explain how changing one weight changes the layer's output.
prerequisites: Has heard the term neural network
learningOutcomes: Compute a weighted sum from inputs, weights and a bias
Describe what a sigmoid activation does to that sum
Explain how one weight controls how much one input matters
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners three inputs, three weights and a bias on paper and ask for the weighted sum and roughly what the sigmoid output will be.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Multi-slider live computation with visible arithmetic
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Making a black box transparent by printing every intermediate value
pedagogical.feedbackType: The full weighted-sum expression, the activation value, and output-node brightness
misconceptionsAddressed: That a neuron does something more exotic than multiply, add and squash
That the bias is a minor detail rather than a shiftable threshold
discussionQuestions: What does a negative weight mean about an input's role?
Why squash the output into a range at all?
If training adjusts weights, what is the network actually learning?
